behaviours.title: An account never seen has balance 0 and no entries
behaviours.given: a new Ledger with no accounts
behaviours.then: the balance is 0 and the entries list is empty
behaviours.contrary_then: reading an unknown account's balance gives undefined instead of 0
contrary_alternatives: reading an unknown account throws an 'unknown account' error
the account is created on read and appears in the ledger

behaviours.title: A deposit of 100 raises the balance to 100 and records a deposit entry
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('a') is 100 and entries('a') is [{ txnId: 'd1', kind: 'deposit', amount: 100 }]
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is refused because account 'a' was never opened, and the balance stays 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted but a fee is deducted so the balance is below 100
the deposit is rejected with 'unknown-account'

behaviours.title: Deposits of 0, -5 or NaN are rejected as invalid-amount and do not use up the txnId
behaviours.when: deposit('a', 0, 'x'), deposit('a', -5, 'y') and deposit('a', NaN, 'z') are called, then deposit('a', 5, 'x')
behaviours.then: the first three return { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }; the later deposit reusing 'x' succeeds and the balance is 5
behaviours.contrary_then: a deposit of 0 is accepted as a no-op with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: a negative deposit is accepted and reduces the balance to -5
the rejected txnId 'x' is remembered so the later deposit of 5 is silently ignored and balance stays 0

behaviours.title: Repeating a deposit with the same txnId succeeds but credits only once
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance stays 100 with a single entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the repeat is credited again and the balance becomes 200
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with reason 'duplicate'
the repeat is credited again with two entries

behaviours.title: txnIds are shared across operation types: a withdrawal reusing a deposit's txnId is silently ignored
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } but nothing is withdrawn; the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal goes through (txnIds are separate per operation) and the balance becomes 49.5
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected with reason 'duplicate' and the balance stays 100

behaviours.title: Amounts are rounded to the cent half-up: 10.005 becomes 10.01
behaviours.then: the balance is 10.01 and the entry amount is 10.01
behaviours.contrary_then: the amount is rounded down (floating point) and the balance is 10
contrary_alternatives: the amount is kept unrounded and the balance is 10.005
the deposit is rejected for having more than two decimals

behaviours.title: A deposit of 0.004 rounds to 0 cents yet is accepted with a zero entry
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance is 0 and one entry of kind 'deposit' with amount 0 is recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is refused as too small and no entry is recorded
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rounded up to 0.01

behaviours.title: Opening an account that already exists keeps its balance and history
behaviours.then: the balance stays 100 and the entry is still there
behaviours.contrary_then: re-opening resets the account to balance 0 with no entries
contrary_alternatives: re-opening throws an 'account exists' error

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit of 100 at rate 1.5 credits 150 as a deposit
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance is 150 and the entry is { txnId: 'f1', kind: 'deposit', amount: 150 }
behaviours.contrary_then: the rate is applied as a divisor and the balance is 66.67
contrary_alternatives: the original amount 100 is credited ignoring the rate
a conversion fee is taken and less than 150 is credited

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit with rate 0 or amount -1 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: both return { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the rate-0 deposit is accepted and credits 0
contrary_alternatives: the rate-0 deposit is rejected with 'amount-too-small' instead

behaviours.title: A foreign deposit converting to under half a cent is rejected as amount-too-small; half a cent is accepted as 0.01
behaviours.then: the first returns { ok: false, reason: 'amount-too-small' }; the second returns { ok: true } and the balance is 0.01
behaviours.contrary_then: the 0.001 deposit is accepted and credits 0 with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the 0.005 deposit is also rejected as too small (rounding half-down)
the 0.001 deposit is rounded up to 0.01

behaviours.title: Repeating a foreign deposit with the same txnId credits only once
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance stays 150
behaviours.contrary_then: the repeat is credited again and the balance becomes 300
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: Withdrawing 50 from 100 charges a 1% fee of 0.50, leaving 49.50
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance is 49.5 and the withdrawal entry amount is 50.5 (principal plus fee)
behaviours.contrary_then: no fee is charged and the balance becomes 50
contrary_alternatives: the fee is recorded as a separate entry of 0.5
the withdrawal is refused

behaviours.title: Withdrawing 10 charges the minimum fee of 0.50, not 1% (0.10)
behaviours.then: the balance is 89.5
behaviours.contrary_then: a plain 1% fee of 0.10 is charged and the balance is 89.9
contrary_alternatives: no fee is charged and the balance is 90
a minimum fee of 1.00 is charged and the balance is 89

behaviours.title: A fractional-cent fee is rounded up: withdrawing 123.45 costs a fee of 1.24
behaviours.then: the fee is 1.24 and the balance is 875.31
behaviours.contrary_then: the fee is rounded down to 1.23 and the balance is 875.32
contrary_alternatives: the fee is rounded to nearest (1.23) and the balance is 875.32

behaviours.title: An exact whole-cent fee is not rounded up: withdrawing 100 costs exactly 1.00
behaviours.then: the balance is 899
behaviours.contrary_then: the fee is bumped by a cent to 1.01 and the balance is 898.99
contrary_alternatives: no fee is charged and the balance is 900

behaviours.title: The withdrawal fee is capped at 25: withdrawing 3000 costs 25, not 30
behaviours.then: the balance is 6975
behaviours.contrary_then: the uncapped 1% fee of 30 is charged and the balance is 6970
contrary_alternatives: the fee is capped at 20 and the balance is 6980

behaviours.title: A withdrawal whose amount fits the balance but whose fee does not is rejected
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted because 99.50 is within the balance, leaving -0.50
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted and the fee is reduced to fit, leaving 0
the withdrawal is accepted with the fee waived, leaving 0.50

behaviours.title: A withdrawal that takes the balance to exactly 0 including fee is allowed
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected as insufficient-funds because it would empty the account, and the balance stays 50.5
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted but the fee is not charged, leaving 0.50

behaviours.title: A withdrawal rejected for insufficient funds can be retried with the same txnId
behaviours.given: account 'a' has balance 10 and withdraw('a', 20, 'w1') was rejected as insufficient-funds
behaviours.when: 20 more is deposited and withdraw('a', 20, 'w1') is called again
behaviours.then: the retry returns { ok: true } and the balance is 9.5
behaviours.contrary_then: the retry is treated as a duplicate and ignored, leaving the balance at 30
contrary_alternatives: the retry is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: Withdrawing exactly the daily limit of 5000 is allowed; one more cent that day is refused
behaviours.then: the first returns { ok: true } leaving 4975 (fee 25); the second returns { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and the balance stays 4975
behaviours.contrary_then: the limit is exclusive so the 5000 withdrawal itself is refused with 'daily-limit' and the balance stays 10000
contrary_alternatives: the second withdrawal of 0.01 is also accepted
the fee counts toward the limit so the 5000 withdrawal is refused

behaviours.title: A single withdrawal of 5000.01 exceeds the daily limit and is refused
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and the balance stays 10000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes 4974.99
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is partially fulfilled up to 5000

behaviours.title: The daily withdrawal limit is tracked per account
behaviours.given: accounts 'a' and 'b' each have balance 10000 and 'a' has withdrawn 5000
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and 'b' has balance 9899
behaviours.contrary_then: the limit is shared across the ledger, so 'b' is refused with 'daily-limit' and keeps 10000

behaviours.title: When a withdrawal is both unaffordable and over the daily limit, insufficient-funds is reported
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the daily limit is checked first and the reason is 'daily-limit'

behaviours.title: A withdrawal of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero withdrawal is accepted and the minimum fee of 0.50 is charged, leaving 99.5
contrary_alternatives: the zero withdrawal is accepted as a no-op with { ok: true }

behaviours.title: Repeating a withdrawal with the same txnId deducts only once
behaviours.then: both return { ok: true } and the balance is 89.5
behaviours.contrary_then: both withdrawals are applied and the balance is 79
contrary_alternatives: the second call is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: A transfer of 30 moves exactly 30 with no fee and records out/in entries
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }; 'a' has 70 with a last entry { txnId: 't1', kind: 'transfer-out', amount: 30 }; 'b' has 30 with entries [{ txnId: 't1', kind: 'transfer-in', amount: 30 }]
behaviours.contrary_then: a withdrawal-style fee of 0.50 is charged and 'a' ends with 69.5
contrary_alternatives: the transfer is refused because 'b' was never opened

behaviours.title: A transfer of the whole balance is allowed; one cent more is refused
behaviours.then: the first returns { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } with balances unchanged; the second returns { ok: true } leaving 'a' 0 and 'b' 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the 100.01 transfer is accepted and 'a' goes to -0.01
contrary_alternatives: transferring the whole balance is refused so 'a' keeps 100

behaviours.title: A transfer of -5 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and 'a' keeps 100, 'b' has 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the negative transfer is accepted and moves 5 from 'b' to 'a', making 'a' 105
contrary_alternatives: it is rejected with 'insufficient-funds' because 'b' has nothing

behaviours.title: Repeating a transfer with the same txnId moves the money only once
behaviours.given: account 'a' has balance 100 and transfer('a', 'b', 30, 't1') was made
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }; 'a' stays 70 and 'b' stays 30
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is applied again: 'a' becomes 40 and 'b' 60
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: Splitting 10 among three recipients gives the leftover cent to the first: 3.34, 3.33, 3.33
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }; 'a' has 90 with a 'split-out' entry of 10; 'b' gets 3.34, 'c' 3.33, 'd' 3.33, each as a 'split-in' entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the leftover cent goes to the last recipient: 'b' 3.33, 'c' 3.33, 'd' 3.34
contrary_alternatives: the leftover cent stays with 'a', so 'a' has 90.01 and each recipient 3.33
each recipient gets 3.33 and the cent is lost

behaviours.title: Splitting 0.02 among three gives 0.01, 0.01 and 0 in recipient order
behaviours.then: 'b' gets 0.01, 'c' 0.01, 'd' gets 0 but still has a 'split-in' entry of amount 0; 'a' has 0.98
behaviours.contrary_then: the split is refused because a share would be zero, and 'a' keeps 1
contrary_alternatives: 'd' receives no entry at all
the cents go to the last two recipients: 'b' 0, 'c' 0.01, 'd' 0.01

behaviours.title: A split with no recipients is rejected as no-recipients, even if its txnId was already used
behaviours.then: both return { ok: false, reason: 'no-recipients' } and 'a' keeps 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the call reusing 't1' is treated as a duplicate and returns { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the empty split is accepted as a no-op with { ok: true }

behaviours.title: A split of 0 with no recipients reports invalid-amount first
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the recipients are checked first and the reason is 'no-recipients'
contrary_alternatives: the split is accepted as a no-op

behaviours.title: Repeating a split with the same txnId pays out only once
behaviours.given: account 'a' has balance 100 and split('a', ['b', 'c'], 10, 's1') was made
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }; 'a' stays 90 and 'b' stays 5
behaviours.contrary_then: the split is applied again: 'a' becomes 80 and 'b' 10
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: A split of the whole balance is allowed; one cent more is refused
behaviours.then: the first returns { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } with 'a' still 10; the second returns { ok: true }, 'a' is 0 and 'b' and 'c' each 5
behaviours.contrary_then: the 10.01 split is accepted and 'a' goes to -0.01
contrary_alternatives: splitting the entire balance is refused so 'a' keeps 10

behaviours.title: A year of 5% interest on 1000 credits 50 as an interest entry
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, the balance is 1050 and the last entry is { txnId: 'i1', kind: 'interest', amount: 50 }
behaviours.contrary_then: a 360-day year is used and the balance becomes 1050.69
contrary_alternatives: interest is compounded daily and the balance becomes 1051.27

behaviours.title: 30 days of 5% interest on 1000 is 4.10, rounded down from 4.1096
behaviours.then: the balance is 1004.1
behaviours.contrary_then: the interest is rounded to nearest (4.11) and the balance is 1004.11
contrary_alternatives: a 360-day year gives 4.17 and a balance of 1004.17

behaviours.title: Interest that rounds to 0 returns ok, records nothing, and leaves the txnId reusable
behaviours.then: the interest call returns { ok: true } with no new entry and balance still 1; the later deposit with 'i1' is credited and the balance becomes 6
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero-interest call consumes 'i1', so the later deposit is ignored and the balance stays 1
contrary_alternatives: the interest call is rejected with 'amount-too-small'
a zero-amount interest entry is recorded

behaviours.title: Interest with rate 0 or 0 days is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: both return { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and the balance stays 1000
behaviours.contrary_then: both are accepted as no-ops with { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: a negative or zero rate is accepted and charges the account

behaviours.title: Repeating interest with the same txnId credits it only once
behaviours.given: account 'a' has balance 1000 and applyInterest('a', 5, 365, 'i1') was applied
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and the balance stays 1050
behaviours.contrary_then: the interest is applied again on 1050 and the balance becomes 1102.5
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with reason 'duplicate'
